question.problem: What is the domain of the function $f(x)=3\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3})-1?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is given by

$$
x\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $3\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-\frac{\pi }{3})-1,$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(x-\frac{\pi }{3}).$ This gives

$$
x-\frac{\pi }{3}\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-\frac{\pi }{3} & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi +\frac{\pi }{3} \\ x & \ne \frac{5\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne \frac{5\pi }{6}+n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.
